question.text: This 1854 act created the two namesake territories and allowed them to decide whether to become slave states using the doctrine of popular sovereignty.
question.clue: Josiah Miller and R.G. Elliott organized the Sandbank Convention as a consequence of the passage of this act, which also stimulated the activity of the Emigrant Aid Company.

swap.leadin: This general's "neckties" were formed using railroad rails he destroyed in one campaign.
swap.text: Name this general, who made use of scorched earth tactics in his "March to the Sea".
swap.clue: This military leader issued "Special Field Orders Number 15," demanding parcels of 40 acres be given to freed slaves.

question.text: This May 2-4, 1862 battle in Virginia saw the Union under Gen. Hooker defeated by the Confederates, under Gen. Lee. It was notable as the site of the death of Thomas "Stonewall" Jackson.
question.clue: Occurring at the intersection of the Orange Plank Road and Orange Turnpike, it saw Early man Marye's Heights to isolate Sedgwick.

swap.text: The Liberator was published by Isaac Knapp and this man, who infamously burned a copy of the Constitution in 1854, calling it an "Agreement with Hell" for its support of slavery.
swap.clue: Arthur and Lewis Tappan splintered from one society started by this man.

question.leadin: William Henry Seward's "Higher Law" speech opposed it.
question.text: Name this compromise which admitted California into the Union as a free state in exchange for a national Fugitive Slave Act.
question.clue: Texas agreed to place its northern border at 36o30' and relinquished its claims to New Mexico.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the merchant Wilmer McLean and his unique role in the Civil War.
swap.text: McLean's house was used as the headquarters for this Confederate general during the First Battle of Bull Run. His order to fire at Fort Sumter began the Civil War.
swap.clue: Near the end of the Civil War, he was given command of the Department of the West, but clashed with John Bell Hood, failed to stall Sherman, and was replaced with Joseph Johnston.

question.leadin: Answer these questions about the history of an oft-overlooked minority -- black Canadians.
question.text: Many blacks took this network of routes and abolitionist households to come to Canada, where they stayed. Its operation was aided by William Still and Harriet Tubman.
question.clue: This organization spread information with the folk song "Go Down Moses."

swap.text: In reaction to the raid on Lawrence, Kansas by border ruffians, Brown and local militia perpetrated this event, killing 5 pro-slavery settlers.
swap.answerHtml: Pottawatomie Massacre [accept reasonable equivalents mentioning an attack in Pottawatomie]
swap.clue: Henry Clay Pate briefly captured some of this event's perpetrators, but then surrendered to the others at the Battle of Black Jack.

question.leadin: Answer the following about the history of impeachment in the U.S., per part.
question.text: Andrew Johnson was impeached in 1868 for violating the Tenure of Office Acts by dismissing of this Secretary of War.
question.clue: Lorenzo Thomas was selected to replace this man in one post during an ordeal that violated the Tenure of Office Act.

swap.leadin: Abraham Lincoln's brother-in-law Benjamin Hardin Helm was killed at this battle.
swap.text: Name this 1863 battle fought in northern Georgia during which Thomas J. Wood created a hole in the Union line after moving his division to fill a nonexistent gap.
swap.clue: By ordering his troops to stand and fight on Snodgrass Hill, George Thomas averted a complete disaster, which earned him the sobriquet "The Rock of" this battle.

question.leadin: Mike Royko coined a nickname of a politician with this last name, "Moonbeam," from his then-girlfriend Linda Ronstadt.
question.text: Name this last name of a politician who proposed Jesse Jackson as a running mate in the 1992 presidential election. That politician with this last name served as governor of California like his father, Pat, who lost to Reagan.
question.answerHtml: Brown [accept Jerry Brown or Edmund Gerald Brown Jr; accept Pat Brown or Edmund Gerald Brown]
question.clue: The death of Elijah (+) Lovejoy prompted a man of this surname to state, "I consecrate my life to the destruction of slavery."

swap.text: This Confederate was appointed as commander of the Army of Tennessee over Joseph Johnston in 1864; he then rather unsuccessfully conducted the Atlanta campaign against Sherman and lost to George Thomas at Nashville.
swap.clue: His rapid attacks saved the Southern army from severe defeat first at South Mountain and then at Antietam, after which he as promoted the army's youngest major general.

question.text: After attacking Confederate-held Pinos Altos, Mangas Coloradas unsuccessfully attempted an alliance with a Confederate officer from this family who captured Mesilla. This family names a private university in Waco, Texas.

swap.leadin: Stonewall Jackson's troops took a detour to take over this garrison on their way to join Lee before Antietam.
swap.text: Identify this garrison where three years earlier Lee led US Marines in the capture of a man who had raided the arsenal for weapons to incite a slave rebellion.
swap.clue: The Secret Six backed a raid in this location by an abolitionist in 1859.

question.leadin: In this decade, a U.S. cavalry detachment massacred a group of Cheyenne and Arapaho gathered at Sand Creek in Colorado.
question.text: Name this decade in which Red Cloud organized a namesake war against the U.S. in Wyoming. During this decade, the Dakota War ended with the largest mass execution in American history.
question.clue: The Treaty of Fort Laramie concluded a war in this decade named for Oglala Lakota chief Red Cloud.

swap.leadin: Answer some questions about the history of Mississippi.
swap.text: Union General Ulysses S. Grant's army captured this Mississippi town on the 4th of July, 1863 after a two-month siege, marking a turning point in the Civil War.
swap.clue: Following the capture of the state capital, John Pemberton was forced to retreat to this city but was unable to harry Union forces after their seizure of the Yazoo River.

question.leadin: Identify these Speakers of the House from descriptions FTPE.
question.text: This Virginian once declared to his son "I am a Southern man." Whatever, dude. He served as speaker from 1839-41 and later as secretary of state in the Confederacy. He was an organizer of the Confederate delegation to the Hampton Roads conference.

swap.text: One of Porter's lieutenants in his Polynesian escapades was this man, who became the first US Navy Admiral, and gave the order "Damn the torpedoes" before attacking the Confederate fleet at Mobile Bay.
swap.clue: A World War I recruiting poster depicted this man defiantly pointing as he is lashed to the mast.

question.leadin: Answer the following about court cases regarding the authority of the executive branch and originating from the Civil War.
question.text: This group of cases, decided in a 5-4 decision delivered by Robert Grier, found that Lincoln's call for a blockade before Congress could declare war was legal. Moreover, this decision gave Lincoln freehand to continue to conduct the war as he saw fit without fear of judicial undermining.

swap.text: A leader of the USSC was George Templeton Strong, who wrote a diary about the war. Another diarist of the period is this better known South Carolina woman, who described the Confederate perspective. The diaries of both Strong and this woman frequently appear in Ken Burns' The Civil War series.
swap.clue: This woman, a prominent Charleston socialite whose husband was an aide to Jefferson Davis, wrote an extensive diary of the Civil War, published posthumously by her friend Isabella Martin under the 1905 title A Diary from Dixie.
